correctness.rationale: For deterministic two-island bias-one no-self-weight map B(z,s)=zs/[zs+(1-z)(1-s)], drift sign is that of s-1/2. Starting (x,1-x), 1/2<x<1, both drifts are nonnegative for r>=h and nonpositive for r<=1/h, with strict drift by the second iterate even at equality; cooperative monotonicity and exclusion of interior coordinate limits force consensus (1,1) or (0,0). The polarized corner has diagonal multipliers 1/(hr),r/h, so for 1/h<r<h it attracts a neighborhood of complementary data. At r=h, writing e=1-u and v the minority opinion, the exact 1/v reciprocal increment is 2(1-v)(v-e)/[v(1-e+v)]. Geometric decay e<=delta q^t and telescoping yield T_eta(delta)=(2delta)^-1+O(log(1/delta)) for fixed h,eta. Independently numerically checked h=1.5 and h=3 at delta=0.005,0.001, obtaining delta T near 0.52 then 0.505-0.506; exact drift/reciprocal identities were also checked from algebra. This is not a theorem for stochastic/heterogeneous networks or uniformly h->1.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS for the inclusive unequal-size demographic global takeover and universal inverse-seed delay. Dandekar–Goel–Lee analyze equal-sized homophilous islands r=1; their polarization theorem is not an unequal-size takeover theorem. Xia et al. treat stability and consensus for broader networks, and local corner multipliers are credited, but their inspected local stability result and all-one-side consensus premise do not imply an initially opposed two-island global r>=h criterion or the 1/(2delta) critical-time law.
residual_risks: Alternative monotone-system analyses of unequal communities may recover the same bifurcation or parabolic passage law under different notation.
Central ratio regime only proves existence of polarized basin, not global convergence to polarization for all initial complements.
